_about: D-066 — the patterns behind his human-reader feedback, round 1. AUTHORED: the grouping, the names, the reasons and the suite proposals with what each costs and what speaks against it, and the audit (A1) the check proposals share (all DRAFT — nothing lands in the suite before his 'land it'). GENERATED elsewhere, never typed here: how many of his items and of the review's findings each pattern holds (from legibility-feedback.md tags and review-r1.raw.json 'pattern' fields through the two maps below), and the before / after numbers of each check (measures.*.json). A reviewer tag missing from reviewTagMap stops the page's build.

patterns.name: The hover describes the kind, not the item
patterns.line: One item had several hovers, each told a third of it, and most said what every item of its kind is. Two different items read the same.
patterns.whyModel: A model reads every hover at once, beside the data record that tells items apart. Repetition costs it nothing, and the fact that separates two twins sat in the record.
patterns.whyHuman: A person sees one hover at a time and has to compare them from memory. A definition repeated on every item hides the one line that is about this item.

suite.what: Report nested hover targets, a hover line repeated on many items (a legend candidate), and two items in one cell or list whose hovers or faces read the same.
suite.lands: three counts in the audit — hovers inside a hover, a line many hovers repeat, twins in one cell — each with a case that fires and a case that stays silent in its battery
suite.against: A line many hovers repeat is sometimes right, a legend line for instance, so each flag needs a look before a fix; on all-endpoints it starts with a long list.

suite.what: A hover opens with what makes THIS item itself, in before · checks · gives order. What a kind means lives once, in a legend.
suite.lands: skills/gabe-lens/references/lens-spec.md (the plain mode) and skills/gabe-artifact/SKILL.md, one rule each
suite.against: A rule in words alone; P10 says such a rule breaks on the next surface unless a check stands behind it (P1.1).

patterns.name: The page talks about itself
patterns.line: Hovers said where the page took a colour or an icon, and what the map could not read. Nothing in them was about the code.
patterns.whyModel: Where a fact came from matters to the model that built it; it is true and it is the model's own concern. The rule against it (D-017) was written down but nothing checked it.
patterns.whyHuman: A person reads the page to learn the code. A sentence about the page is noise that sits where the answer should be.

suite.target: the legibility audit (A1) + the words sweep of each page generator (gen-all-endpoints.py, gen-legibility-review.mjs)
suite.what: Stop words about the page or the map (as the table draws it, found by, the map does not, my proposal outside an option) in hovers and faces.
suite.lands: a count of hovers about the page in the audit, and a stop-list in each generator's words sweep
suite.gate: The audit reports; the words sweep stops the build.
suite.against: Some panels are about the map on purpose (THE GAPS, R-07); the stop-list needs a way to mark them, or it stops a page you want.

suite.target: the gabe-artifact rules (and later the execution contract)
suite.what: State D-017 for every generated page: what the code does is shown; how the map knows it is not.
suite.against: Alone it is a rule in words; it holds only with the check of P2.1 behind it.

patterns.name: An element drawn without its identity
patterns.line: Gates, functions and client branches were bare words: no icon, no kind, no role. A row had no icon of its own.
patterns.whyModel: The model knows what a thing is from its key. The page drew an icon only where the Gabe Universe draws a node, a rule that made sense to the generator.
patterns.whyHuman: A bare word is an unknown thing. He had to ask what each one was.

suite.what: Every item in a row of elements wears an icon: the station's, or a page mark that the legend declares. Gates follow what you rule for gate icons: if you rule no icon, gates are left out of the count.
suite.lands: a count of bare items in the audit, with its two battery cases
suite.against: An icon on every item can crowd a dense row; the count says where an icon is missing, not whether the row needs one.

suite.target: the gabe-artifact rules + the station conventions
suite.what: A kind the station does not draw gets a page mark, never a plain word; one kind, one look, on every surface of a page.
suite.against: A page mark for every kind grows the legend; on a small page that is more to learn than the bare word.

patterns.name: One end of a relation
patterns.line: A condition without the function that checks it, a refresh without what it fetches, a branch shown as a file and a line, tables without the function that touches them.
patterns.whyModel: The data record joined both ends: a data chip carried the table AND the function. The page drew one end; the model reads the keys, not the face.
patterns.whyHuman: A person reads the face. Half a relation is a question: checked where? fetched from what? written by whom?

suite.target: each page generator, as a build check (gen-all-endpoints.py, gen-legibility-review.mjs)
suite.what: An element whose record joins two things draws both ends, or its hover names the other end.
suite.lands: a check in the build of each generator, beside its words sweep
suite.against: The generator must say which records join two things; a join it does not list stays unchecked.

suite.what: A role word needs its object: a fetcher OF what, a check IN which function, a branch ON which ending.
suite.lands: skills/gabe-lens/references/lens-spec.md, one rule in the plain mode
suite.against: Words only; no check stands behind it.

patterns.name: Structure hidden in a mark, or mixed into an axis
patterns.line: A stage mark whose meaning was only in a hover, a column of timeless facts inside a timeline, names broken in the middle of a word, text cut off, counts with no noun.
patterns.whyModel: The model reads the mapping and the widths as data. It never sees the pixels, the wrap or the line where a name breaks.
patterns.whyHuman: A person sees the pixels. A mark without a key and a word cut in half both stop the reading.

suite.what: No word broken between two letters (camel humps, _ . / allowed); no text clipped, a closed selector's text included; a timeline's heads are all moments; a grid's heads do what you rule for the heads, scrolled.
suite.lands: skills/gabe-artifact/tools/verify-artifact-chrome.mjs grows by these checks, and tests/artifact-chrome by a case for each
suite.gate: It fails the render gate, which runs before a publish.
suite.against: A gate that fails on a cut word holds back a page you may want published as it is; today it would fail all-endpoints on its bench selectors (R-10).

suite.what: A mark carries a visible key; a number carries its noun; an axis holds one kind of thing.
suite.against: Words only; P5.1 is the check behind it.

patterns.name: One thing, several names (and one name, several things)
patterns.line: The same thing went by several names: deciders, deciding functions, or no name at all; the screen, what sends it, the screen sends it. One word, request, stood for a kind and for a lifetime. Every member he missed was drawn, under another name.
patterns.whyModel: The model holds all the vocabularies and the key that joins them, so three names for one thing still resolve.
patterns.whyHuman: A person matches by words. A second name reads as a second thing; one word for two things reads as one.

suite.target: the legibility audit (A1), reading each page's words file
suite.what: One display word per concept across a page's views; two concepts never share a display word on one page.
suite.lands: a count in the audit that reads a page's words file for one display word on two concepts, or two on one
suite.against: Telling two concepts apart from their words alone is a guess; it will flag words that only look alike, and each flag needs your look.

suite.what: Extend 'one term per concept' from prose to the words a page shows.
suite.against: The register is a trial in this repo; a rule there reaches no other project yet.

patterns.name: The code's spelling instead of its meaning
patterns.line: str(exc) as an answer, 'only when not (existing is not None)', a pydantic error type as a rule, a feed id or an i18n key on a face.
patterns.whyModel: The model reads code as fluently as prose, so the expression IS the meaning to it.
patterns.whyHuman: A person, even a programmer, has to decode each one — and str(exc) is not the message at all.

suite.what: Faces and hovers never show a raw feed id, a library error id or a source expression as a value.
suite.lands: a count of raw feed words on faces and hovers in the audit
suite.against: A raw word is sometimes the only name there is; the count needs a list of the names you want to keep.

suite.what: The meaning first, in words; the code last, as written.
suite.against: Words only; P7.1 is the check behind it.

patterns.name: A word or a number that promises more than its rule
patterns.line: 'sends no headers' when the headers were not read; 'proves' on a test that only fits; a count whose rule is not the one its label says; a Python set's add drawn as a database write.
patterns.whyModel: The model knows the rule it computed and reads the label as a handle for it.
patterns.whyHuman: A person reads the label literally. When the rule is looser than the words, the page tells him something false.

suite.target: each page generator, as a build check (gen-all-endpoints.py, gen-legibility-review.mjs)
suite.what: A count's label comes from the same definition that computes it; unknown is never drawn as none. The state words: unknown · absent · beyond one level, where a bare 0 or [] stood (the element-forms state-word sweep, docs/design/element-forms/review-a4.md, fix 6).
suite.lands: a check in the build of each generator
suite.against: The check can hold a label to its rule only where the generator states both; a label typed into a template stays unchecked.

suite.what: The same state words — unknown · absent · beyond one level, where a bare 0 or [] stood (docs/design/element-forms/review-a4.md, fix 6) — carried from the forms feed to generated pages.
suite.against: A clause in the execution contract reaches every skill at once, so its wording needs a review of its own.

patterns.name: No bench to decide one element's look
patterns.line: Every element was drawn at once in a dense table before any one element's look had been decided alone.
patterns.whyModel: A model needs no look to understand an element, so the dense view came first.
patterns.whyHuman: A person decides a look by seeing one element, its parts and its controls, before seeing eighty of them.

suite.what: A bench step — one element per column, its parts and its controls — before a dense view of many.
suite.lands: skills/gabe-mockup/references/spike.md gains a bench step, and the method note here says it too
suite.gate: A step to follow: nothing runs.
suite.against: A bench costs a page of its own before the dense view; for an element whose look is already settled it is a detour.

patterns.name: A written rule with no check breaks on the next surface
patterns.line: Choices made alone that were not options, options the copy text dropped, a typed number, lifted words that skipped the words sweep, text under the size floor, an unruled look drawn as ruled.
patterns.whyModel: Every agent was told the rules. Rules that a check enforced held (typed numbers in the words file, twin hovers once the check existed); rules that lived only in words broke on the new surfaces.
patterns.whyHuman: He cannot re-check every rule on every page. A rule he has to remember to check is the rule that breaks.

suite.target: each page generator (gen-all-endpoints.py, gen-legibility-review.mjs) + the legibility audit (A1)
suite.what: Every standing rule of a generated page gets a check on a rail that already runs (the build, the probe, the commit gate): an option is in the copy text, a pick is marked, a lifted string goes through the words sweep, text keeps the floor.
suite.lands: checks in the build and the probe of each generator, and in the audit
suite.gate: The build checks stop the build; the audit reports.
suite.against: A check per rule grows each generator; a rule that is cheap to keep by eye may not be worth its check.

suite.what: A page rule without a check is not a rule: when a rule is written, its check is named in the same change.
suite.against: The clause is itself a rule in words; it holds only if a review asks for the check.

audit.name: The legibility audit: measure-legibility.mjs moved into the suite
audit.what: One script opens a generated page in a browser and counts each kind of defect this round found. Today it is a prototype in this folder, run by hand on all-endpoints. Landed, it takes any page, and the check proposals marked part of A1 become its counts.
audit.lands: skills/gabe-artifact/tools/legibility-audit.mjs, moved from docs/design/design-context/legibility/measure-legibility.mjs, and a new battery, tests/legibility-audit/run.sh, that proves each count can fire and stay silent
audit.battery: suite-doctor gains one more battery that opens a browser, so its run grows.
audit.against: It reads one page at one width; a defect that shows on another endpoint or at another width stays unseen. Its first run on all-endpoints is a long list of work, not a pass.
